f.title: Use the FAERS Electronic Submissions web page for the full set of IND safety report submission documents
f.statement: The technical specifications associated with the guidance are separate documents updated periodically; for a complete listing of all documents and supportive files needed to submit IND safety reports to FAERS, the sponsor refers to the FAERS Electronic Submissions web page.
f.clause: Related documents

f.title: Submit in-scope IND safety reports to FAERS in accordance with this guidance
f.statement: Under section 745A(a) of the FD&C Act, the guidance requires sponsors to submit IND safety reports for serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions required under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(i), submitted to CDER or CBER, to FAERS in accordance with the guidance, thereby changing the electronic submission requirements for this category of reports.
f.clause: I. Introduction
f.applicability: IND safety reports submitted to CDER or CBER for serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(i)

rows.quote: This guidance implements the electronic submission requirements of section 745A(a) of the FD&C Act for the electronic format of the content submitted for IND safety reports that are required under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(i) for serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions. This guidance applies to IND safety reports that are submitted to the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) or the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER). This guidance changes the electronic submission requirements for this category of IND safety reports by requiring sponsors to submit the IND safety reports to FAERS in accordance with this guidance.
rows.location: I. Introduction
rows.review_note: Review: statement wording aligned to quote ('changes' rather than 'replacing'). Mandatory kept ('requiring', 745A(a)). Double-check: quote proves 'requiring sponsors to submit ... to FAERS', CDER/CBER and 312.32(c)(1)(i) scope; Mandatory confirmed.

f.title: Keep submitting IND safety reports under the eCTD guidance until the FAERS requirement takes effect
f.statement: Until the requirements in this guidance become effective, the most recent effective version of the eCTD guidance continues to apply to sponsors electronically submitting IND safety reports for serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions.
f.clause: I. Introduction

rows.quote: Until the requirements in this guidance become effective, the most recent effective version of the eCTD guidance will continue to apply to sponsors electronically submitting IND safety reports for serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions.

f.statement: During the voluntary submission program, if sponsors choose to submit IND safety reports to FAERS, they should no longer submit those IND safety reports in eCTD format.

f.title: Once effective, submit in-scope IND safety reports electronically in the specified format unless exempt or waived
f.statement: Once the requirement is effective, sponsors of INDs subject to this guidance are required to submit IND safety reports electronically in the format specified in the guidance, unless the sponsor is exempted from the electronic submission requirements (section III.C) or a waiver is obtained (section IV.D).
f.clause: I. Introduction
f.exceptions: Sponsors exempted from the electronic submission requirements (section III.C); sponsors that obtain a waiver (section IV.D)

f.title: Apply the FAERS electronic format requirement to all 7- and 15-day SUSAR IND safety reports
f.statement: The guidance applies only to IND safety reports for serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions required under 21 CFR 312.32(c), which includes both the 7- and 15-day reporting requirements depending on the severity of the event; under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(i), sponsors must report any suspected adverse reaction that is both serious and unexpected if there is evidence to suggest a causal relationship between the drug and the adverse event.

f.applicability: 7-day and 15-day IND safety reports for serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions

rows.quote: This guidance applies only to IND safety reports for serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions required under 21 CFR 312.32(c), which includes both 7- and 15-day reporting requirements depending on the severity of the event (see 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(i), (c)(2)). Under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(i), sponsors must report any suspected adverse reaction that is both serious and unexpected if there is evidence to suggest a causal relationship between the drug and the adverse event, such as in the following circumstances:

f.title: Exclude other IND safety report types from the FAERS electronic format requirement
f.statement: The guidance does not apply to IND safety reports for anything other than serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions covered by 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(i) and (c)(2); examples of excluded reports are findings from other studies (312.32(c)(1)(ii)), findings from animal or in vitro testing (312.32(c)(1)(iii)) and increased rate of occurrence of serious suspected adverse reactions (312.32(c)(1)(iv)).
f.clause: III.B. Types of Submissions for Which the Electronic Submission Requirement Does Not Apply

rows.quote: This guidance does not apply to IND safety reports for anything other than serious and unexpected suspected adverse reactions covered by 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(i) and 21 CFR 312.32(c)(2). Below are examples of IND safety reports for which the requirements of this guidance do not apply: 6 − Findings from other studies, as required under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(ii) − Findings from animal or in vitro testing, as required under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(iii) − Increased rate of occurrence of serious suspected adverse reactions, as required under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(iv)

f.title: Exclude IND safety reports for CBER-regulated devices licensed as biologics from this guidance
f.statement: The guidance does not apply to IND safety reports for devices that are regulated by CBER as biological products under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act and that require submission of an IND before submission of a biologics license application.
f.clause: III.B. Types of Submissions for Which the Electronic Submission Requirement Does Not Apply
f.applicability: Devices regulated by CBER as biological products under PHS Act section 351

f.title: Noncommercial INDs are exempt from the FAERS electronic submission requirement
f.statement: FDA has exempted all submissions regarding noncommercial INDs from the requirements under section 745A(a) of the FD&C Act.
f.clause: III.C. Types of Submissions That Are Exempted From the Electronic Submission Requirement

f.title: Treat investigator-sponsored and expanded access INDs as noncommercial INDs for the 745A(a) exemption
f.statement: For purposes of the section 745A(a) exemption, a noncommercial IND is an IND for a product that is not intended for commercial distribution and includes investigator-sponsored INDs and expanded access INDs (e.g., emergency use INDs and treatment INDs).
f.clause: III.C. Types of Submissions That Are Exempted From the Electronic Submission Requirement
f.applicability: Noncommercial INDs, including investigator-sponsored INDs and expanded access INDs (emergency use and treatment INDs)

f.title: Noncommercial IND sponsors are encouraged to use the FAERS format for IND safety reports
f.statement: Although noncommercial INDs (and associated IND safety reports) are exempt from section 745A(a), FDA encourages sponsors of noncommercial INDs to submit IND safety reports using the format described in the guidance.
f.clause: III.C. Types of Submissions That Are Exempted From the Electronic Submission Requirement

f.title: Comply with the FAERS submission requirement from April 1, 2026
f.statement: The requirement to submit IND safety reports as described in the guidance becomes effective 24 months after publication of the guidance in the Federal Register (April 1, 2026); FDA accepts IND safety report submissions as described in the guidance before that date.
f.clause: IV.A. Timetable for Implementation of Electronic Submission Requirements

rows.deadline: Effective 24 months after publication of the guidance in the Federal Register (April 1, 2026)

FDA will accept IND safety report submissions as described in this guidance before the date that the requirement is in effect as noted in section I., Introduction.
rows.location: IV.A. Timetable for Implementation of Electronic Submission Requirements

f.title: Submit IND safety reports to FAERS through the ESG or the Safety Reporting Portal
f.statement: Sponsors must submit IND safety reports to FAERS using either the Electronic Submission Gateway (ESG) or the Safety Reporting Portal (SRP); sponsors using the ESG consult the FDA Data Standards Catalog for the ICH E2B data standard currently supported by FDA.
f.clause: IV.B. Specifications for Submission of IND Safety Reports to FAERS
f.systems: FAERS; FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG); Safety Reporting Portal (SRP); FDA Data Standards Catalog; ICH E2B

rows.quote: Sponsors must submit IND safety reports to FAERS using either the Electronic Submission Gateway (ESG) or the Safety Reporting Portal (SRP). For sponsors using the ESG, consult the FDA Data Standards Catalog 10 for information about the ICH E2B data standard currently supported by FDA.
rows.location: IV.B. Specifications for Submission of IND Safety Reports to FAERS

f.statement: Before submitting an IND safety report to FAERS for the first time, whether through the ESG or SRP, the sponsor should create an account with FDA if one has not been previously established; to create an account, the sponsor should notify the FAERS electronic submission coordinator.
f.clause: IV.C. Presubmission Considerations
f.exceptions: Not needed if an account has already been established

f.title: Optional FAERS test submissions; no coordinator contact needed for subsequent reports
f.statement: The FAERS coordinator helps the sponsor create an account, ensures that all steps for successful submission have been completed and provides instructions for optional test submissions; it is not necessary to contact the FAERS coordinator before submitting subsequent IND safety reports in electronic format.
f.clause: IV.C. Presubmission Considerations

f.title: Temporary waivers of FAERS submission may be granted only in defined circumstances
f.statement: FDA may grant temporary waivers of the requirement to submit certain IND safety reports in FAERS if extraordinary events or circumstances beyond the submitter's control justify a waiver (including natural disasters that impact computer operations), or if an unplanned, long-term internet disruption or other unplanned event (e.g., malware attacks) would preclude the sponsor from submitting in FAERS.
f.clause: IV.D. Waiver Requests
f.exceptions: Waivers are temporary and anticipated only in rare circumstances

rows.quote: Section 745A(a)(2) of the FD&C Act allows FDA to establish criteria for waivers from the electronic submission requirements. The Agency anticipates that temporary waivers will be needed only in rare circumstances. FDA may grant temporary waivers of the requirement for submission of certain IND safety reports in FAERS, as described in this guidance, if one or more of the following events or circumstances exist: 13 • Extraordinary events or circumstances occur that are beyond the control of the submitter that justify a waiver, including but not limited to natural disasters that impact computer operations • An unplanned, long-term internet disruption or other unplanned event occurs that would preclude the sponsor from submitting in FAERS (e.g., malware attacks)
rows.location: IV.D. Waiver Requests

f.clause: IV.D.1. Content of Waiver Requests

f.statement: If the waiver is granted, FDA generally includes in its response letter the alternate submission method(s) it intends to accept and the time frame for the waiver; waivers of the requirement to submit to FAERS, if granted, are temporary, apply only to the requestor and are not transferable to another sponsor.
